title: Uniformly bounded derived towers with pro-zero cohomology are pro-zero
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ and cohomology functors $H^q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $X_n\in D(\mathcal A)$ for $n\geq1$ and let $t_{k,n}:X_k\to X_n$ for $k\geq n$ satisfy $t_{n,n}=\mathrm{id}$ and $t_{\ell,n}=t_{k,n}\circ t_{\ell,k}$ for $\ell\geq k\geq n$. Suppose there are fixed integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^q(X_n)=0$ for every $n$ and every $q\notin[a,b]$. Suppose also that for each integer $q$ and each $n\geq1$ there exists $k\geq n$ with $H^q(t_{k,n})=0$. Then for each $n\geq1$ there exists $k\geq n$ with $t_{k,n}=0$ in $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 0G3B (lemma-essentially-constant-cohomology), specialization to essentially constant cohomology systems with value zero

proof.text: Fix $n$. For each $q$, choose $k_q\geq n$ with $H^q(t_{k_q,n})=0$. Since only finitely many degrees $q\in[a,b]$ can be nonzero, choose $k\geq n$ dominating all $k_q$. Then every cohomology map $H^q(t_{k,n})$ is zero; outside $[a,b]$ both groups vanish by the boundedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0G3B, hypotheses (1) and (2), specialized to zero-valued systems

proof.text: Apply the canonical truncation triangle functorially to each $X_n$ at degree $a$: $\tau_{\leq a}X_n \to X_n \to \tau_{\geq a+1}X_n \to (\tau_{\leq a}X_n)[1]$. Functoriality makes these into inverse systems of distinguished triangles, and under the canonical identification $\tau_{\leq a}X_n\cong H^a(X_n)[-a]$ the lower transition is $H^a(t_{k,n})[-a]$. Because $H^q(X_n)=0$ for $q<a$, the lower truncation is isomorphic to $H^a(X_n)[-a]$, so its transition maps are eventually zero by Step 1. The upper truncations have cohomology in the shorter interval $[a+1,b]$.

source.place: Tag 0G3B, proof: truncation distinguished triangle and induction on $b-a$

proof.text: Induct on $b-a$. The base case $b=a$ identifies each $X_n$ with $H^a(X_n)[-a]$, hence the transition is zero. For the induction step, the lower truncation system is pro-zero and the upper truncation system is pro-zero by induction; the zero-valued two-out-of-three lemma for inverse systems of distinguished triangles then gives a later index $k$ with $t_{k,n}=0$.
